title: Which of these four squares have four in the units place?
description: The video finds which of four squares end in the digit four, using the last digit of each number. It then puts one answer back into the question to check it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the units digit of a square comes from squaring the units digit of the number. Watch for students who square the whole number and make a slip, or who pick numbers that themselves end in four.

video_script.why: The child applies the last digit method of the solved example to find squares ending in four.
video_script.substitution: Square the last digit of each number and read the last digit of that result.
video_script.anchor: the four numbers sixty four, one hundred eight, two hundred ninety two and thirty six, each with a square sign
video_script.payoff_line: The squares of one hundred eight and two hundred ninety two end in four

final_answer.spoken: the squares of one hundred eight and two hundred ninety two

never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: the units digit of a square depends only on the units digit of the number
64 ends in 4 and 4 × 4 = 16, so 64² ends in 6; 36 ends in 6 and 6 × 6 = 36, so 36² ends in 6
108 ends in 8 and 8 × 8 = 64, so 108² ends in 4; 292 ends in 2 and 2 × 2 = 4, so 292² ends in 4
video_script.design: One idea: only the last digit matters. The four numbers stay in the anchor band, and the two that qualify are ticked.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Here are four squares. Sixty four squared, one hundred eight squared, two hundred ninety two squared and thirty six squared.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of them have the digit four in the units place?

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Use the same method as for the squares ending in six.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Look at twenty three times twenty three. Its last digit comes from the last digit of the number alone.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers squared are sixty four, one hundred eight, two hundred ninety two and thirty six.

beats.on_screen: To find: which squares end in 4

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which of these squares end in four.

marks.last: each number shrinks to its last digit: 4, 8, 2 and 6

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step one, only the last digit of each number matters. The last digits are four, eight, two and six.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, sixty four ends in four, and four times four is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Thirty six ends in six, and six times six is thirty six. Both squares end in six.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Step three, one hundred eight ends in eight, and eight times eight is sixty four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two hundred ninety two ends in two, and two times two is four. Both squares end in four.

marks.check: 108 × 108 = 11664 is written and its last digit is ringed

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. One hundred eight times one hundred eight is eleven thousand six hundred sixty four, which ends in four.

marks.ans: the two squares are ticked and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The squares of one hundred eight and two hundred ninety two end in four.
